get.summary: `GET /.well-known/jwks.json` — serve every stored signing key's public half.
get.description: Active and rotated-out verify-only keys alike.

200.description: RFC 7517 JSON Web Key Set

get.summary:
`GET /authorization/browser-sessions` — every live browser session (neither revoked nor
expired), newest first, with the caller's own marked by the `sid` its token
carries. Acquired through [`LiveBrowserSessionsReader`] (scope
`wildflower/BrowserSession.r`); the caller's `sid` comes from its own
session through [`LiveSessionReader`].

200.description: Every live browser session, newest first

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

delete.summary:
`DELETE /authorization/browser-sessions/{sid}` — revoke a browser session, which ends
everything minted under it: the browser's own token, and every access
token and refresh family an app it signed in to holds. The caller's own
session may be revoked, which signs that browser out. Acquired through
[`LiveBrowserSessionsRevoker`] (scope `wildflower/BrowserSession.d`).

204.description: The session is revoked, with everything minted under it

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No unrevoked browser session has that `sid`

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

get.summary:
`GET /authorization/clients` — every registered OAuth client (seeded or trusted on first
use), disabled ones included, ordered by `clientId`. Acquired through
[`LiveClientsReader`] (scope `wildflower/Client.r`).

200.description: Every registered client

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

patch.summary:
`PATCH /authorization/clients/{clientId}` — disable (stamped with the server's now,
whatever time is sent) or re-enable a client by writing its `disabledAt`;
answers with the client as stored. A disabled client is refused at
`/oauth/authorize` and `/oauth/token`. Idempotent (a client that already
has a `disabledAt` keeps it). Disabling an essential client — the host
app's or the browser-session client — is refused with `409 EssentialClient`.
Acquired through [`LiveClientsDisabler`] (scope `wildflower/Client.u`).

200.description: The client as stored

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No client with that id

409.description: The client is essential: disabling it would leave the Owner no way in

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

get.summary:
`GET /authorization/devices/{userCode}` — load a pending device-code consent prompt for
the launcher to render (scope `wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r`).

parameters.name: userCode
parameters.description: The code the device page shows

200.description: The pending device or pairing request, for the device page

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No pending device or pairing request has that user code

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/devices/{userCode}/approve` — the Owner approves a device-code
consent prompt, granting the (expanded) scope set and leaving a standing
device grant. Gated by [`LiveConsentDecider`] (scope
`wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`), which also carries the approver's own
scopes: an approval delegating a resource scope beyond them is rejected with
a `403`. The write scope lives in the consent capability's `approve_device_consent`.

parameters.name: userCode
parameters.description: The code the device page shows

200.description: The request is decided: `approved`, or `denied` when nothing was left to grant

403.description: The caller's token lacks an approval scope, or a ticked resource scope is beyond the approver's own grant; nothing is written

404.description: No pending device or pairing request has that user code

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/devices/{userCode}/deny` — the Owner declines a device-code consent
prompt (scope `wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`).

parameters.name: userCode
parameters.description: The code the device page shows

200.description: The request is declined: always `denied`

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No pending device or pairing request has that user code

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

get.summary:
`GET /authorization/grants` — every standing grant, of both kinds, in the
order they were granted: what each app or device has been allowed and
keeps. Acquired through [`LiveGrantsReader`] (scope `wildflower/Grant.r`):
the read capability *is* the extractor, so the scope check can't be
skipped.

200.description: Every standing grant, in the order granted

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

get.summary:
`GET /authorization/grants/{id}` — one standing grant, or `404` when no
grant has the id. Through `Scoped<LiveGrantsReader>`
(`wildflower/Grant.r`).

200.description: The grant

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No grant has that id

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

delete.summary:
`DELETE /authorization/grants/{id}` — revoke a grant, expire the
refresh-token families minted under its client, and bump the client's
revocation epoch so any still-live *access* tokens die too — no
`offline_access` client (or a leaked live bearer) outlives the revocation.
Acquired through [`LiveGrantsRevoker`] (scope `wildflower/Grant.d`), which
owns the whole cascade, so it doesn't also take `wildflower/Token.d`.
`204 No Content`, or `404` when no grant has the id.

204.description: The grant is revoked, with every token its client holds

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No grant has that id

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/logout`: denylist the presented token's `jti`
through `Authenticated<LiveSessionEnder>`, then answer `303 See Other` to
the hosted launcher's root. No scope gates it.

303.description: The token is revoked, best-effort: a store failure is logged and the logout goes ahead

get.summary:
`GET /authorization/oauth-consents/{id}` — load a pending authorization-code consent
prompt for the launcher to render (scope `wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r`).

200.description: The pending request, for its consent card

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No pending code-flow request the card may load has that id: unknown, decided, expired, still waiting on its browser's limited page, or for a client disabled since

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/oauth-consents/{id}/approve` — the Owner approves a
consent prompt, granting a (narrowed) scope set and minting the authorization code the
polling endpoint hands back to the client. Gated by [`LiveConsentDecider`]
(scope `wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`), which also carries the approver's
own scopes: an approval delegating a resource scope beyond them is rejected
with a `403`. Approving a prompt whose client, redirect, or scopes are
outside the current registration without
[`acknowledged_registration_change`](ApproveOAuthConsentBody::acknowledged_registration_change)
is rejected with a `409` and writes nothing, as is an approval naming a
patient other than the one the request's SMART launch binds. The write
scope lives in the consent capability's `approve_oauth_consent`.
post.description:
The answers:

- `200`, `"status":"approved"`: the code is issued; `redirect` is the
  app's callback carrying it and the app's `state`, for the card to leave
  for.
- `200`, `"status":"denied"`: nothing was granted, the requesting
  browser's session has ended, or the app was disabled since; the request
  is denied and `redirect` carries `access_denied`.
- `403`: the approver lacks an approval scope, or a ticked resource scope
  is beyond their own grant. Nothing is written.
- `409`: the registration change wasn't acknowledged, or the body names a
  patient other than the one the launch bound. Nothing is written.
- `404`: no live code-flow prompt has this id.

200.description: The request is decided: `approved` with the app's callback carrying the code, or `denied` with the callback carrying `access_denied` when nothing was granted, the requesting browser's session has ended or the app was disabled since

403.description: The caller's token lacks an approval scope, or a ticked resource scope is beyond the approver's own grant; nothing is written

404.description: No pending code-flow request has that id

409.description: The registration change wasn't acknowledged, or the body names a patient other than the one the launch bound; nothing is written

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/oauth-consents/{id}/ask-owner` — a browser that can read a consent
prompt but not approve it hands it to the server's Owner (scope
`wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r`, as reading it takes): the request no
longer counts as decidable in the browser that made it, so the host
notifies the Owner. Decides nothing. Raising a request spends from the
authorization start limit, as starting one the Owner is asked about does:
`429 Too Many Requests` when refused, the request left as it was. Raising
one already raised spends nothing. `204 No Content`, or `404` once the
request is no longer pending.

204.description: The request is raised for the Owner, by this call or an earlier one

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No pending code-flow request has that id

429.description: The authorization start limit refused raising the request; it is left as it was

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/oauth-consents/{id}/deny` — the Owner declines a consent prompt (scope
`wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`). The answer carries the client callback
with `error=access_denied`, for the consent card to leave for.

200.description: The request is declined: `denied`, with the app's callback carrying `access_denied`

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No pending code-flow request has that id

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/revocations`, through `Scoped<LiveTokenRevoker>`
(`wildflower/Token.d`): denylist one token or bump a subject's epoch.
`204 No Content` on success; `400` with `error` and `detail` for a body that
names neither mode, both, a `jti` without `expiresAt`, or an `expiresAt`
already past.

204.description: The token is denylisted, or the subject's tokens are revoked

400.description: The body names neither mode, both, a `jti` without `expiresAt`, or an `expiresAt` already past

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

500.description: The revocation store failed; logged, with no body

get.summary:
`GET /authorization/session`: the caller's own scopes and its browser
session's expiry, read from its claims through
`Authenticated<LiveSessionReader>`, which no scope gates.

200.description: The caller's own scopes and its browser session's expiry

500.description: The browser session store failed; logged, with no body

get.summary:
`GET /authorization/session-widenings/{id}` — load a pending session
widening for its card (scope `wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r`).

200.description: The pending widening, for its card

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No pending widening has that id: unknown, decided or expired

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/session-widenings/{id}/approve` — the Owner approves
a session widening, and the browser's session grows by what was granted.
Gated by [`LiveConsentDecider`] (scope
`wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`), which also carries the approver's
own scopes: granting a scope beyond them is a `403`.

200.description: The widening is decided: `approved` when the session grew, `denied` when nothing was left to grant or the browser's session has ended

403.description: The caller's token lacks `wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`, or a ticked scope is beyond the approver's own grant; nothing is written

404.description: No pending widening has that id: unknown, decided or expired

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /authorization/session-widenings/{id}/deny` — the Owner declines a
session widening, leaving the browser's session as it was (scope
`wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`).

200.description: The widening is declined: always `denied`

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover the scope this operation requires

404.description: No pending widening has that id: unknown, decided or expired

500.description: A store failed; logged, with no body

get.summary:
The authorization endpoint (RFC 6749 §3.1), the public front door of the
OAuth flow. It issues nothing to a browser without a browser session: such
a browser is sent to the pairing page first. For a browser with one it
validates the request, then either auto-issues an authorization code (when
an existing grant pre-approves every requested scope) or parks the
user-agent on the consent card or the wait page while the Owner decides.
get.description:
Nothing in-process calls this route. Registered clients (e.g.
SMART-on-FHIR apps) discover it via the FHIR server's
`.well-known/smart-configuration` (`authorization_endpoint`) and send the
*user's browser* here with PKCE params to start an authorization-code
flow:

1. Browser lands here. The browser session cookie is read before anything
   else: a browser without a live browser session is 302'd to the pairing
   page, `/oauth/pair?next=<this request's path and query>`, and nothing is
   parked, notified or consumed. Once the Owner approves the pairing, the
   page sends the browser back here with its new session. A browser with a
   session has its request parked as an `AuthorizationRequest` (5-minute
   TTL), made in that session (`sid`). A SMART App Launch's `aud` and
   `launch` are checked first (see their fields), and the launch is
   consumed onto the request.
2. A request asking for more than the browser's session holds (scopes a
   code issued in that session would not carry in full) waits on the
   limited page at `/oauth/authorize/{id}/limited`, which says what the
   session lacks and offers Continue or Cancel:
   `POST /oauth/authorize/{id}/continue` goes on as below,
   `POST /oauth/authorize/{id}/cancel` answers the client
   `access_denied`. Until then the Owner isn't asked about it. Once a
   browser session has pressed Continue for a client, its later requests
   for that client skip the page, whatever the session then lacks, unless
   the request carries `prompt=consent`. From the page the browser can
   also ask the Owner to widen its session
   (`POST /oauth/authorize/{id}/ask-to-widen`). What the session holds is
   read from its row, which an approved widening has grown.
3. Unless every requested scope is pre-approved by an existing grant for
   this (client, `redirect_uri`) pair, the request joins the pending-consent
   queue and the browser is 302'd to a page this authorization server
   serves beside the endpoint, on the origin the browser used. A browser
   whose session can decide consents and holds the request's approval
   scopes goes to the consent card at `/oauth/authorize/{id}/consent`, where
   it decides in place; the request records that it can be decided there
   (`decidable_in_requesting_browser`). Any other goes to the wait page at
   `/oauth/authorize/{id}/wait`, and the Owner is notified (the host
   webview's popup). The wait page polls `GET /oauth/authorize/{id}` (a
   custom extension, not part of any RFC), which answers the browser
   session the request was made in and a session that can decide it on
   the consent card, until the Owner decides — in the
   popup, in a signed-in launcher, or on the consent card once that
   browser can decide it. Either way the code is issued under the session
   the request was made in, not the approver's.
   RFC 6749 leaves the owner-interaction mechanism unspecified, so both
   pages are spec-legal; likewise §4.1 explicitly allows skipping consent
   on a previously established authorization decision, which is what the
   grant fast path implements.
4. Approval 302s the browser back to the client's `redirect_uri` with
   `code` + `state` (§4.1.2); the client then redeems the short-lived
   code at `POST /oauth/token` (§4.1.3) with its PKCE verifier.

Clients without a server-defined registration are **trusted on first use**: an
unknown `client_id`, an unregistered `redirect_uri`, and scopes outside the
registration are all carried to the Owner's prompt as a registration warning
rather than rejected here, and nothing is written to the `clients` table
until the Owner approves. Such a request never takes the grant fast path,
and while its redirect is untrusted every other failure renders the local
HTML page instead of redirecting. A server-defined registration (the host
app's, the FHIR server UI's) keeps the strict treatment, and a disabled
client is rejected either way. Once the redirect is trusted, a failure goes
back to the client's `redirect_uri` with `error`, `error_description` and
`state` (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1) instead.

The start limit is asked only when it must be: its layer defers a request
from a browser that can decide consents, and one carrying no session, and
the starter asks the deferred limit only before it raises the request for
the Owner or parks it for the limited page.

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description:
The response the client wants; only `code` is supported, anything else
is `unsupported_response_type`.

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: The PKCE transform (RFC 7636 §4.3); only `S256` is accepted.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description:
The client asking. An unknown one is trusted on first use and carried
to the Owner's prompt as a registration warning; a disabled one is
refused on a local page.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description:
The scopes asked for, space-separated (RFC 6749 §3.3). Scopes outside a
trusted-on-first-use client's registration are carried to the Owner's
prompt; outside a server-defined registration they are refused.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description:
The PKCE challenge, `BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier))`, which the code
remembers so `POST /oauth/token` can check the verifier (RFC 7636 §4.2).

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description:
Where the browser goes back to with the code or the error. It must be
an http(s) URL; until it is trusted (registered for this client), a
failure renders the local page rather than redirecting there.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
The client's opaque value, carried back unchanged on every redirect to
it. Required here, though RFC 6749 only recommends it.

parameters.name: launch
parameters.description:
SMART App Launch `launch` value, handed to the app in its launch URL
and forwarded here. It must name a launch this server minted for this
`client_id` that is unused and unexpired (five minutes); it is consumed,
so it works once, and the request carries the launch's context
(including any patient it binds) to the consent. Any other value is
`invalid_request`, its `error_description` saying why. A browser
without a session is sent to pairing before the launch is
read, so pairing never spends it. Absent, the request is plain OAuth.

parameters.name: aud
parameters.description:
SMART App Launch audience: the FHIR server the app expects to call with
the token. When present it must be this server's origin
(`https://<domain>`), which is also its FHIR base, else
`invalid_request`. The minted token's `aud` is the server's origin.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description:
OpenID Connect `prompt`, space-separated. Only `consent` means
anything here: a request whose browser session holds less than it asks
for stops at the limited page even when that session has gone on past
the page for this client before, so the browser can ask the Owner to
widen its session. Any other value, and `consent` for a request the
session holds all of, changes nothing.

302.description: Redirect to the pairing page (a browser without a browser session), the limited page (a session holding less than the request asks for), the client redirect_uri, or the authorization server's consent card (a session that can approve the request) or wait page

429.description: The authorization start limit refused the request

get.summary:
Return the current status of the pending authorization request, including
the final redirect URL once approved. The caller's browser session (its
`__Host-browser_session` cookie) is answered when the request was made in
it, or when its grant covers `wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r` and `.u`,
the scopes that decide the request on the consent card. Any other caller,
with another session or none, gets the same `404` as an unknown id, so a
leaked request id can't collect the code.
get.description:
The answers, by where the request stands:

- pending: `200` [`AuthorizationStatus::Pending`];
- pending past its expiry: `200` [`AuthorizationStatus::Error`];
- denied: `200` [`AuthorizationStatus::Denied`], with the client's
  `access_denied` callback;
- approved: `200` [`AuthorizationStatus::Approved`], with the client's
  callback carrying the code;
- unknown, or not readable by this caller: `404`
  `AuthorizationRequestNotFound`;
- approved but with no code: `500` `server_error`, an invariant the store
  broke.

Only code requests are answered here; a device and a pairing have polls of
their own.

The error side is `axum::response::ErrorResponse` because two error shapes
share the handler: the Owner-surface `AuthorizationServerError` (its
`AuthorizationRequestNotFound` 404 / logged 500) and the OAuth-shaped
`OAuthErrorResponse` `server_error` — `?` converts either through its
`IntoResponse`.

200.description: Current authorization-request status

404.description: No authorization request with that id the caller's browser session may read

500.description: Server error (RFC 6749 §5.2)

post.summary:
Ask the Owner to widen this browser's session by what it lacks of request
`id`, which waits on this browser's limited page, and raise the Owner's
notification. The widening asks for exactly what the session lacks of the
request, and the request keeps waiting on the page until the widening's
approval can no longer be collected. Asking again while that widening
still waits for the Owner answers it, and notifies no one. A new widening
spends from the authorization start limit, as a request raised for the
Owner does; a refusal is the limit's `429`, nothing filed.

200.description: The widening waiting for the Owner: filed by this ask, or by an earlier one for the same request

404.description: No request with that id waits on this browser's limited page, or this browser's session lacks nothing it could be widened by

429.description: The authorization start limit refused a new widening

500.description: A store failed, or the browser's session couldn't be verified; logged, with no body

post.summary:
Cancel request `id`: deny it and send the browser back to the app with
`error=access_denied`. Cancel isn't remembered: this session's next request
for the app stops at the limited page again.

200.description: The client callback carrying error=access_denied

404.description: No request with that id waits on this browser's limited page

post.summary:
Go on with request `id` although this browser's session holds less than it
asks for: issue a code under a standing grant that covers it, or else ask
the Owner, on the consent card when this browser can decide it and on the
wait page otherwise, with the request's five minutes started again. The
request spent from the authorization start limit when `/oauth/authorize`
parked it, so going on spends nothing. This browser session's later
requests for the same app skip the limited page. A client disabled since
the request parked ends it: the request is denied and the app is sent
`access_denied`.

200.description: Where the browser goes next: the client callback (with a code, or with error=access_denied when the client was disabled since), the consent card or the wait page

404.description: No request with that id waits on this browser's limited page

get.summary: What this browser's session lacks of request `id`, and the app asking.

200.description: The app and the scopes this browser's session lacks

404.description: No request with that id waits on this browser's limited page

post.summary:
Issue a `(device_code, user_code)` pair for the client to poll on while the
user pairs the device. `Ok` carries the §5.1 cache suppression via
[`DeviceAuthorizationResponse`], `Err` via [`TokenError`].
post.description:
The extractors run in order: the start limit first, before the body is
read, since every device request is raised for the Owner whoever sends it
(a refusal is the `429`); then the `User-Agent`; then [`TokenRequest`],
last because it consumes the body, which checks the content type, parses
the payload and authenticates the client.

200.description: Device + user code pair (RFC 8628 §3.2)

post.summary:
Poll a browser pairing. The poll that finds it approved starts the
browser's paired session and sets it as the browser's
`__Host-browser_session` cookie. A blank `browser_name` keeps the name the
pairing has. An unknown pairing code is a `404`; a store failure, a session
that couldn't be stored, and a token that couldn't be minted are each a
logged `500`.

200.description: Where the pairing stands

Set-Cookie.description: The browser's paired session token as its `__Host-browser_session` cookie, set only when the status is `approved`

404.description: No pairing has the pairing code

500.description: A store failed, the paired session couldn't be stored, or its token couldn't be minted; logged, with no body

post.summary:
Start a browser pairing for this browser, named after its `User-Agent`,
and raise the Owner's notification. The body's `next` is where the browser
goes once paired, in practice the `/oauth/authorize` request it was sent
away from.
post.description:
The answer's pairing code is the page's secret, and the user code is for
the Owner, who confirms it on the device page: only the page that started
the pairing can collect the session. The refusals:

- `next` is no path on this server: `400`, `BrowserPairingNextNotAllowed`.
- The browser-session client is disabled: `403`,
  `BrowserSessionClientDisabled`.
- No unused user code could be generated, or a store failed: a logged
  `500`.

200.description: The started pairing

400.description: `next` is no path on this server

500.description: No unused user code could be generated, or a store failed; logged, with no body

post.summary:
Revoke the presented token. RFC 7009 §2.2: `200` whether the token was
revoked, was already dead, or was never one of this client's.

200.description: Revoked, or not a live token of this client's (RFC 7009 §2.2)

500.description: Server error

post.summary:
Poll the widening `id`, asked in this browser's session. The poll that
finds it approved collects the wider session: it sets the session's new
token as the browser's `__Host-browser_session` cookie and revokes the
token it replaces. A widening of another session's, or none, is a `404`; a
store failure, or a token that couldn't be minted, is a logged `500`.

200.description: Where the widening stands

Set-Cookie.description: The browser's wider session token as its `__Host-browser_session` cookie, set only when the status is `widened`

404.description: No widening asked in this browser's session has that id

500.description: A store failed, the browser's session couldn't be verified, or the wider session's token couldn't be minted; logged, with no body

post.summary:
`POST /oauth/token` (RFC 6749 §3.2, RFC 8628 §3.4): hand the body's grant
to the matching exchange for the authenticated client, an authorization
code with its PKCE verifier, a device code while the device polls, or a
refresh token for an access token and its successor. A `grant_type` the
endpoint doesn't take fails to parse, so it is the extractor's
`400 invalid_request`, "Malformed payload".
post.description:
Either outcome is uncached (§5.1): `Ok` through [`TokenResponse`], `Err`
through [`TokenError`].

200.description: Successful token response (RFC 6749 §5.1)

500.description: Server error (RFC 6749 §5.2)

ApproveBody.description:
Body the device page's consent card posts to
`POST /authorization/devices/{userCode}/approve` to approve a device-code
prompt or a browser pairing: the scopes the Owner ticked, plus an optional
patient context to bind to the grant, and an optional new name for the
device. The card pins a device grant to all patients, so it sends no
`patient` and the field deserializes to `None`.

The code flow posts its own
`ApproveOAuthConsentBody` instead — only that surface can show a
registration warning, and only its body carries the acknowledgement.

approvedScopes.description:
The scopes the approver ticked. They are clamped to what the prompt
may grant and to the approver's own grant; a resource scope beyond the
approver's grant is a `403`, and nothing left to grant is a deny.

patient.description:
The FHIR `Patient` id to bind a device's grant to; `None` leaves it
unbound. A pairing ignores it: a browser session binds no patient.

deviceName.description:
The approver's name for the device or browser, when they changed it
before approving. A device's grant is named after it, else the
device's own name; a pairing names the browser with it. `None` keeps
the name the request carries rather than erasing it.

ApproveOAuthConsentBody.description:
Body posted by the launcher to approve an authorization-code consent prompt.

Its own shape rather than the device flow's
[`ApproveBody`](crate::http::wire_representations::ApproveBody): only this
surface carries a registration warning, so only this body demands the
acknowledgement, and the device flow keeps no field it would always have to
send.

patient.description:
Optional SMART-on-FHIR patient context to bind to the grant. When the
request's SMART launch bound a patient, it must be that patient.

acknowledgedRegistrationChange.description:
The Owner's acknowledgement that they recognise this app and its
redirect address. Required (not defaulted) so a client that has not been
updated to show the warning cannot approve a `new` or `changed` prompt by
omission; it is ignored when the prompt carries no warning.

approvedScopes.description:
The scopes the Owner left ticked. They are clamped to what the browser
asked for and to the approver's own grant; a scope beyond the
approver's grant is a `403`, and nothing left to grant is a deny.

AskedSessionWideningBody.description: The widening an ask filed, which the page polls.

AuthorizationCodeGrant.description:
A standing authorization-code consent: client X may have scopes Y at
redirect URI Z. A later request from the client at that redirect gets its
code without asking the Owner only when it changes nothing in the
client's registration, this grant covers every requested scope, its
browser session is live and holds what it asks for (or its browser has
gone on past the limited page for this client), and a launch's patient,
if any, is this grant's. A grant covering only some scopes pre-ticks them
on the consent card.

One grant per `(client_id, redirect_uri)`. Diesel-mapped 1:1 to the
`authorization_code_grants` table; on the wire it rides inside
[`Grant::AuthorizationCode`].

id.description:
Primary key — a UUID minted at first upsert, unique across BOTH grant
tables (so a bare grant id read through the `grants` view is
unambiguous).

clientId.description: `client_id` the Owner approved this grant for.

scopes.description:
Everything the Owner has approved for this client at this redirect,
across every approval; consent is cumulative (see
[`CumulativeConsent`]).

grantedAt.description:
When the Owner gave (or last re-confirmed) consent: the latest
approval.

lastUsedAt.description:
When this grant last let a code be issued without asking the Owner,
at `/oauth/authorize` or at the limited page's Continue; `None` until
it first does. A re-approval keeps it.

patient.description:
The SMART patient the latest approval named, carried forward to the
codes this grant lets be issued without asking the Owner.

redirectUri.description:
The exact redirect URI this grant covers — `/authorize` keys the
consent-skip fast path on `(client_id, redirect_uri)`.

AuthorizationRequestNotFound.description:
The JSON 404 body an unknown authorization request gets, from the status
poll and from the limited page's calls: also the answer to a caller whose
browser session may not read the request, so the two can't be told apart.

id.description: The request id the caller asked about.

oneOf.description:
`{"status":"pending"}`: undecided and unexpired, whether it waits for
the Owner or still sits on its browser's limited page. The wait page
keeps polling.

`{"status":"denied","redirect":…}`: the Owner declined, or the
browser session the request was made in was revoked; the poll can't
tell the two apart, so every denial reads as declined.

redirect.description:
Client callback URL carrying `error=access_denied`, an
`error_description` and `state` for code-flow requests (RFC 6749
§4.1.2.1) so the wait page can complete the flow. Always set: only
code-flow requests are polled here.

oneOf.description:
`{"status":"approved","redirect":…}`: the request was approved and
its code issued.

redirect.description:
Client callback URL carrying the redeemable `code` and `state`
(RFC 6749 §4.1.2). The wait page follows it.

oneOf.description:
`{"status":"error","message":…}`: the request passed its expiry
undecided, so it can't be decided any more. The wait page stops and
shows the message.

message.description: What the wait page shows: "Authorization request expired".

AuthorizationStatus.description:
Polling response for the wait page watching an authorization request as it
moves from `Pending` toward approval or denial: where the request stands,
and once it is decided, where to send the browser.

BrowserPairingNotFound.description:
No browser pairing has the presented pairing code
(`BrowserPairingNotFound`, 404).

pairingCode.description: The pairing code the start answered with.

browserName.description:
The name the page now gives its browser. Recorded while the request
is pending; blank keeps the name it has.

BrowserPairingRefused.description:
Why a pairing didn't start: `next` is no path on this server
(`BrowserPairingNextNotAllowed`, 400), or the browser-session client is
disabled (`BrowserSessionClientDisabled`, 403).

next.description:
Where the browser goes once it holds its session: a path on this
server, in practice an `/oauth/authorize` URL.

BrowserPairingStatusBody.description:
Where a pairing stands. `approved` carries the browser's session as its
`Set-Cookie`; the page then goes on to its `next`. `slow_down` means the
page polled sooner than its interval.

BrowserSessionBody.description:
A live browser session as the Owner's "Browsers" list reads it. Every
column of the `browser_sessions` row but its `scopes` and `revoked_at`
(always `null` on a live one), plus `heldByCaller`: whether the caller's
own token was minted under it.

sid.description: The session's id, which a revoke names.

kind.description: How the browser got its session: `same_device` or `paired`.

name.description: The name the browser was given; `null` for a same-device session.

createdAt.description: When the browser signed in or was paired.

expiresAt.description: When the session stops letting the browser start things.

lastSeenAt.description:
When the session was last in use, to the nearest
`LAST_SEEN_RESOLUTION`.

heldByCaller.description:
Whether the caller's own token was minted under this session: revoking
it signs the caller's browser out.

BrowserSessionNotFoundBody.description:
Wire shape for `BrowserSessionNotFound` (404) — no standing browser
session has this `sid`.

sid.description: The session id the caller asked for: unknown, or already revoked.

ClientBody.description:
A registered OAuth client as the Owner's "Trusted apps" list reads it. Every
column of the `clients` row **except `secret_hash`**, which never leaves the
server, and `registration_source`, plus `essential` — whether this is the
host app's client or the browser-session client, which can't be disabled,
so the list offers no switch for them.

clientId.description: The public identifier the app sends on every OAuth request.

name.description: The app's display name, shown on the consent card and in this list.

redirectUris.description: Absolute redirect URLs, matched exactly at `/oauth/authorize`.

allowedScopes.description:
The scopes the app may request; a request outside them is refused or,
for an app trusted on first use, shown to the Owner as a change.

allowedGrantTypes.description: The `grant_type` values the client may use at `/oauth/token`.

registeredAt.description: When the app was registered: seeded, or first approved by the Owner.

disabledAt.description: Set while the client is disabled; `null` when it is enabled.

essential.description:
Whether the Owner needs this app to get in (the host app's client or
the browser-session client); disabling it is refused.

ClientNotFoundBody.description:
Wire shape for `ClientNotFound` (404) — no registered client has this
`client_id`.

oneOf.description:
The redirect is registered and every scope is covered: nothing new
for the Owner to acknowledge.

The Owner has never approved this app; nothing about it is stored
until they do.

The app is known, but the request steps outside its registration: a
new redirect, new scopes, or both.

redirectUriIsNew.description: The presented `redirect_uri` is on no allowlist entry.

newScopes.description:
The requested scopes the registration does not cover, in request
order.

ClientRegistrationBody.description:
Wire shape of [`OAuthConsent::registration`] — the
[`PresentedClientChange`], `status`-tagged.

`{"status":"registered"}` for a request that matches the registration,
`{"status":"new"}` for a client this authorization server has never seen, and
`{"status":"changed","redirectUriIsNew":…,"newScopes":[…]}` when a known
client steps outside its registration.

oneOf.description:
The request was approved: a code-flow request's code is issued, a
device's grant stands, a pairing's browser may now sign in.

redirect.description:
The app's callback carrying the code and the app's `state`, for
the consent card to leave for; absent for a device-page decision,
whose device or browser polls for its result.

oneOf.description:
The request was denied: declined, or an approval that granted
nothing. A code-flow approval is a deny too when the requesting
browser's session has ended or the app was disabled since.

redirect.description:
The app's callback carrying `error=access_denied` and the app's
`state`; absent for a device-page decision.

ConsentResult.description:
Result the approving surface sees after approving or denying a consent
prompt: `{"status":"approved"}` or `{"status":"denied"}`, with a
`redirect` for a code-flow decision.

A code-flow decision carries the client callback URL (`code` + `state`, or
`error=access_denied` + `state`, appended to the client's `redirect_uri`) so
the approving surface can complete the flow directly when it is the
requesting browser (the consent card) — no separate poll of
`/oauth/authorize/{id}` needed. Device-flow decisions have no client
`redirect_uri`, so `redirect` is `None` and (thanks to
`skip_serializing_if`) omitted from the wire entirely.

DeviceAuthorizationRequest.description:
`POST /oauth/device_authorization` request body (RFC 8628 §3.1) — the
optional `scope` plus the body credentials, and the non-standard
`device_name` extension. Form-urlencoded.

client_id.description:
The client's id, for `client_secret_post` or a public client; omitted
when it authenticates by `Authorization: Basic`.

client_secret.description:
A confidential client's secret, for `client_secret_post`; never beside
a Basic header.

scope.description:
The scopes the device asks for, space-separated; each must be one the
client may ask for.

device_name.description:
Non-standard: a name for the device, shown to the approver. Without
one, the device is named from its `User-Agent` when that names a
browser or a system.

device_code.description:
The secret the device polls `/oauth/token` with until the Owner
decides. Only the device holds it.

user_code.description:
The short code the device shows its user, which the Owner confirms on
the device page before deciding.

verification_uri_complete.description:
The device verification page with the code filled in,
`{origin}/oauth/device?user_code={user_code}`. The Owner still confirms
the code before the page reads the request.

expires_in.description:
Seconds until the request expires; a poll after that is
`expired_token`.

interval.description:
Seconds the device waits between polls; polling sooner is answered
`slow_down` (RFC 8628 §3.5).

DeviceConsent.description:
Body returned to the launcher when it loads a pending device-page consent
prompt — what asks, the requesting client, the device's or browser's
name, the scopes the approver's ticks start from, and the *expansion
envelope* the approver may grant up to (device consent is expandable): a
device client's full allowed-scope set, a browser's the Owner's scopes.
Local to this one route (its only reader).

kind.description: What asks: `device` for a device's request, `browser` for a pairing.

userCode.description: The code the Owner entered or confirmed, which approve and deny name.

clientId.description:
The requesting client: the device's app, or the browser-session client
for a pairing.

clientName.description: The client's registered name, or its `client_id` when it has no row.

deviceName.description:
The browser's name for a pairing; for a device, the name it gave or
was inferred from its `User-Agent`, if any.

startingScopes.description:
The scopes the approver's ticks start from: a device's requested
scopes, or for a browser everything the caller may delegate.

allowedScopes.description:
How far the approver may expand: the app's whole registered scope
list for a device, the Owner's scopes for a pairing. Device consent is
expandable.

missingApprovalScopes.description:
The approval scopes the caller's own token lacks to approve this
request (`wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`, and `wildflower/Grant.c`
for a device's standing grant). Empty when it may approve; otherwise
the device page sends the Owner to the device running the server.

DeviceConsentKind.description:
What asks at the device page: a device, through the RFC 8628 device-code
flow, or a browser pairing for a browser session. On the wire, `"device"`
or `"browser"`.

DeviceConsentNotFoundBody.description:
Wire shape for `DeviceConsentNotFound` (404) — no pending device-code consent
has this user code. Keyed by `userCode`, unlike the id-keyed siblings.

userCode.description:
The user code the caller asked for: unknown, decided or expired, or a
code-flow request's, which the device page never shows.

DeviceGrant.description:
A standing device pairing: the durable record of an approved device-code
flow, keyed on the client and the human-facing device name. It is the
Owner's record of which devices they have paired; it never skips a prompt.
A refresh family begun by the device's poll records the grant's `id`.
Diesel-mapped 1:1 to the
`device_grants` table; on the wire it rides inside [`Grant::DeviceCode`].

id.description:
Primary key — a UUID minted at first upsert, unique across BOTH grant
tables.

clientId.description: `client_id` the Owner approved this pairing for.

scopes.description:
Scopes the Owner approved; consent is cumulative (see
[`CumulativeConsent`]).

grantedAt.description:
When the Owner gave (or last re-confirmed) consent: the latest
approval.

lastUsedAt.description:
When a refresh-token family this pairing earned last rotated; `None`
until one first does. A re-pairing keeps it.

patient.description: The SMART patient the latest approval named, if any.

deviceName.description:
The human-facing device name this pairing is keyed on. Defaults to
the client's name when the device didn't name itself.

EssentialClientBody.description:
Wire shape for `EssentialClient` (409) — the named client is essential:
disabling it would leave the Owner no way in.

clientId.description:
The essential client the caller tried to disable: the host app's or
the browser-session client.

allOf.description:
A standing consent for a client at one redirect, tagged
`authorization_code`.

oneOf.description:
A standing consent for a client at one redirect, tagged
`authorization_code`.

Grant.description:
The wire/list seam over the two concrete grant kinds — what cross-kind
reads (`all_grants`, `grant_by_id`) return and what the `/authorization/grants`
endpoints serialize. Internally-tagged on `grantType` with the snake_case
kind names, so each variant serializes as its struct's camelCase fields
with the tag alongside — the exact `grantType`-tagged union the TS
`access-management` `GrantSchema` decodes (pinned by the tests below).

GrantNotFoundBody.description: Wire shape for `GrantNotFound` (404) — no standing grant has this id.

id.description: The grant id the caller asked for.

InsufficientScopeBody.description:
Wire shape for a 403 — the caller authenticated, but their token doesn't cover
the scope(s) an operation requires. `missingScopes` names the scopes the
caller must additionally hold.

error.description: Always `"InsufficientScope"` — the discriminant a client switches on.

missingScopes.description: The rendered scopes the caller lacks.

Jwks.description: RFC 7517 JSON Web Key Set body served at `/.well-known/jwks.json`.

keys.description:
Every stored signing key's public half, the active key and the
rotated-out keys kept to verify tokens they signed alike.

LaunchPatientMismatchBody.description:
Wire shape for `LaunchPatientMismatch` (409) — the approval named a patient
other than the one the request's SMART launch binds.

id.description: The id of the request whose approval was refused; nothing was written.

OAuthConsent.description:
Body returned to the launcher when it loads an authorization-code consent
prompt — describes the client, scopes, and any pre-approved subset. Local to
this one route (its only reader); the shapes two consent surfaces share live
in [`crate::http::wire_representations`].

id.description: The request's id, which the card approves or denies by.

clientName.description:
The client's registered display name, so the consent UI can name the
app instead of showing a raw `client_id`. Falls back to the
`client_id` when the registration lookup misses.

scopes.description: Everything the app asked for, in request order.

redirectUri.description: Where the app will be sent back to with the code.

preApprovedScopes.description:
The requested scopes a standing grant already covers, ticked to start
with.

patient.description:
The patient on the request's approval. A request the card can load is
pending, so it carries no approval and this is `null`; the patient a
SMART launch bound is not sent. The field stays on the wire so the card
can be told of a patient a request asks for, once a launch can.

registration.description:
How this request compares against the client's registration **right
now** — the warning the consent UI leads with, and the flag that makes
its acknowledgement checkbox mandatory.

missingApprovalScopes.description:
The approval scopes the caller's own token lacks to approve this
request (`wildflower/Grant.c`, and `wildflower/Client.c` or
`wildflower/Client.u` when approving would register or widen the
client). Empty when it may approve; otherwise the consent UI asks the
server's Owner in place of Allow.

oneOf.description:
The approval steps outside the app's registration without the
Owner's acknowledgement.

The approval names a patient other than the one the request's SMART
launch binds.

OAuthConsentApprovalConflictBody.description:
The `409` an approval is refused with, writing nothing: either body, told
apart by its `error`. Only the spec reads it; each is rendered from its
own [`AuthorizationServerError`] variant.

OAuthConsentNotFoundBody.description:
Wire shape for `OAuthConsentNotFound` (404) — no pending authorization-code
consent has this id.

id.description:
The request id the caller asked for: unknown, decided, expired, still
waiting on its browser's limited page, or for a client disabled since.

OAuthError.description:
RFC 6749 §5.2 error body: the token, revocation and device-authorization
endpoints, the wait page's status poll, and client authentication all
answer with it.

error.description:
The standard error code, such as `invalid_request` or
`invalid_client` (an [`OAuthErrorCode`]'s wire string).

error_description.description:
A sentence for the app's developer saying what was wrong; omitted when
the code says enough.

PolledConsentResult.description:
[`ConsentResult`] as a polled flow's decision answers it, for the spec: a
device's, a browser pairing's or a session widening's requester polls for
its result, so the decision carries no `redirect`. Only the spec reads it;
the routes render a [`ConsentResult`] with none.

PublicJwk.description:
One signing key's public half, as served at the JWKS endpoint. Resource
servers fetch it to verify the access tokens the server signs.

kid.description: Key identifier matching the source `SigningKey.kid`; verifiers use this to select the key.

alg.description: JWS algorithm the key is intended for — always `"RS256"`.

key_ops.description: Permitted JWK operations — always `["verify"]` for published public keys.

RegistrationNotAcknowledgedBody.description:
Wire shape for `RegistrationNotAcknowledged` (409) — the approval named a
client, redirect, or scope outside the current registration and did not carry
the Owner's acknowledgement.

id.description: The id of the request whose approval was refused; nothing was written.

RevocationRefusedBody.description: The `400` a malformed revocation body gets.

detail.description: A sentence saying what the body should have been.

oneOf.description: Bulk-revoke every token the subject holds that was issued up to now.
Denylist one token until its own expiry.

expiresAt.description: The token's own expiry (RFC 3339), in the future.

RevocationRequestBody.description:
`POST /authorization/revocations` body as the spec describes it: exactly
one of the two modes. Only the spec reads it; the route reads the looser
[`RevocationRequest`] so it can answer each malformed body with its own
`400`.

SessionResponse.description:
What the caller's current access token carries: its scopes, and when the
browser session it was minted under expires. The rest of the claim set
(`jti`/`iss`/`aud`/`patient`) is session plumbing no caller has asked for,
and leaving it off keeps this from drifting into a general introspection
endpoint. Widen it when something actually needs a field.

scopes.description:
The `scope` claim split on whitespace — the scopes this session actually
holds. Empty when the token carries no `scope` claim at all.

browserSessionExpiresAt.description:
When the browser session the token was minted under (its `sid`)
expires; `null` for a token under no browser session.

SessionShortfallBody.description:
What the limited page says: the app, and the scopes this browser's session
lacks of what the app asked for.

clientName.description: The app's registered name, or its `client_id` when it has none yet.

missingScopes.description:
The requested scopes, as the app asked for them, that a code issued in
this browser's session would not carry in full, in the request's order.

SessionShortfallNextBody.description: Where the limited page sends the browser next.

location.description:
The client callback (with a code, or with `error=access_denied`), or a
path on this server: the consent card or the wait page.

SessionWideningConsent.description:
Body returned when the card loads a pending session widening: the browser
that asks, the app it asks for, and the scopes the Owner may grant, which
the Owner may only untick.

id.description: The widening's id, which approve and deny name.

browserName.description: The name of the browser that asks: its session's.

clientId.description: The app whose request the browser's session fell short of.

clientName.description: The app's registered name, or its `client_id` when it has no row.

requestedScopes.description:
What the browser's session lacked of the app's request: the most the
Owner may grant.

startingScopes.description:
The scopes the card's ticks start from: those of the requested ones
the caller may pass on.

missingApprovalScopes.description:
The approval scopes the caller's own token lacks to approve the
widening (`wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u`). Empty when it may
approve.

SessionWideningNotFound.description:
The JSON 404 body a session widening the caller may not see gets: from the
limited page's poll, one asked in another browser session, or none.

id.description: The widening id the caller asked about.

SessionWideningNotFoundBody.description:
Wire shape for `SessionWideningNotFound` (404) — no session widening the
caller may see has this id.

id.description:
The widening id the caller asked for: unknown, decided or expired for
the Owner's card; another session's for the limited page's poll.

SessionWideningStatusBody.description:
Where a widening stands. `widened` carries the browser's wider session as
its `Set-Cookie`; the page then goes on with the app's request.

StartedBrowserPairingBody.description: A started pairing, for the pairing page.

pairingCode.description: The secret the page polls with. Only this page holds it.

userCode.description: The code the page shows, which the Owner confirms on the device page.

browserName.description:
The name the browser goes by until the page names it, taken from its
user agent.

next.description:
Where the page sends the browser once it holds its session: `next`,
resolved against this server.

interval.description: Seconds the page waits between polls.

oneOf.description: Redeem an authorization code with its PKCE verifier (RFC 6749 §4.1.3).

client_id.description:
The client's id, for `client_secret_post` or a public client;
omitted when it authenticates by `Authorization: Basic`.

client_secret.description:
A confidential client's secret, for `client_secret_post`; never
beside a Basic header.

code.description: The code `/oauth/authorize` sent to the client's redirect.

code_verifier.description:
The PKCE verifier whose S256 hash is the request's
`code_challenge` (RFC 7636 §4.5).

redirect_uri.description: The same `redirect_uri` the authorization request named.

oneOf.description: Poll with a device code until the Owner decides (RFC 8628 §3.4).

client_id.description:
The client's id, for `client_secret_post` or a public client;
omitted when it authenticates by `Authorization: Basic`.

client_secret.description:
A confidential client's secret, for `client_secret_post`; never
beside a Basic header.

oneOf.description:
Trade a live refresh token for a fresh access token and the refresh
token's successor (RFC 6749 §6).

client_id.description:
The client's id, for `client_secret_post` or a public client;
omitted when it authenticates by `Authorization: Basic`.

client_secret.description:
A confidential client's secret, for `client_secret_post`; never
beside a Basic header.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token being rotated; it is spent by the trade.

TokenRequestBody.description:
`POST /oauth/token` request body — the `grant_type`-tagged union of the
three grants the endpoint dispatches (mirrors
`super::token_exchange::TokenPayload` plus the body credentials).
Form-urlencoded (RFC 6749 §3.2). `client_id`/`client_secret` are optional:
a confidential client may instead authenticate via `Authorization: Basic`
(RFC 6749 §2.3.1) and omit them from the body — `resolve_client_credentials`
accepts either source.

TokenResponse.description:
RFC 6749 §5.1 successful token-endpoint response: what the token endpoint
gives an app for an authorization code, a refresh token or a device code.

access_token.description: The signed access token (a JWT) the app presents as its bearer.

expires_in.description: How many seconds the access token lives from issue.

scope.description:
The scopes the access token holds, space-separated: the grant's, which
may be narrower than the app asked for.

refresh_token.description:
Present only when the grant carries [`wildflowerhealthio_scopes::KnownScope::OfflineAccess`]
— the plaintext of the freshly-minted refresh-token generation (RFC 6749
§5.1; only its hash is persisted).

patient.description:
The SMART patient context: the FHIR `Patient` id the grant is bound
to. Present only when the grant binds one.

TokenRevocationRequestBody.description:
`POST /oauth/revoke` request body (RFC 7009 §2.1) — the token plus the
body credentials. Form-urlencoded. `token_type_hint` is accepted and not
read: the server tells the token's type from the token.

client_id.description:
The client's id, for `client_secret_post` or a public client; omitted
when it authenticates by `Authorization: Basic`.

client_secret.description:
A confidential client's secret, for `client_secret_post`; never beside
a Basic header.

token.description:
The client's own access or refresh token to revoke. A token that is
unknown, already dead or another client's is answered `200` alike
(RFC 7009 §2.2).

UpdateClientBody.description:
Body of `PATCH /authorization/clients/{clientId}` — the one client field the Owner
can edit.

disabledAt.description:
Any time to disable the client now, or `null` to re-enable it. The
server stamps its own now whatever time is sent, so a disable can't be
scheduled or backdated. Required, `null` included.
